items.title: Loretta Rowland Evans Interview
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] By the way, did you ever know a fellow named Tom Brown? ... [INTERVIEWEE] No, I was living here two years. ... I don't know exactly how long. I lived there, Goodwire on the 16th Constance.

ctx.x: Yeah. We used to sing Stars Bang Havana of course. That's the first song we sang in praise to our flag. We'd all have flowers and every year they still do that. They go off Dr. McDonald's statue. Here's a poem. One I dedicated to my daughter Yvonne. That other one was to my daughter Effie, my little girl. Appreciation. This was written in 1951 I wrote this. And this book has been gone over by a critic. If you see the corrections. Everything's criticized. And told me he's ready for publication. And after that…
By the way, did you ever know a fellow named Tom Brown? He lived in this neighborhood. He was a trombone. But I thought you were trying to think of who some of the new-

No, I was living here two years. I lived on the Louisiana Avenue Annunciation before this. I lived on Sixth Street for quite some years. I don't know exactly how long. I lived there, Goodwire on the 16th Constance.
